citations.claim: first pole_upright violation at step 28, pole angle 0.8295 rad exceeds 0.8 limit
pole already leaning far at step 25 before violation

counterfactual.change: set sensor_noise from 0.01597 to 0, keeping all other fields and 28 steps identical; this removes the failure

explanation: Seeded sensor noise (~0.016) corrupts the state-feedback measurement while the pole starts slightly tilted with negative cart velocity. The controller applies wrong-direction/insufficient corrective force (only ~4.5 at step 20 rising to ~25 at step 28), allowing theta to grow monotonically from 0.027 to 0.427 (step 20) to 0.68 (step 25) to 0.83 (step 28). Removing noise alone stabilizes the run, proving noise-induced mis-estimation is the cause.
vision_note: The pole leans progressively farther to the right from step 25 to 27 while the cart stays near the center without moving underneath it to recover. At step 28 the pole tip turns red at a large lean angle, marking the pole-upright violation.
